svg.title: Diagram of what USPS pages say about Registered Mail, with no prices, fees or insurance amounts. What it is: the most secure USPS mail service, protected by safes, cages, sealed containers, locks and keys; a signature is required on delivery; Registered Mail Restricted Delivery directs delivery only to the addressee or the addressee's authorized agent. Sending it: only at the time of mailing, presented to a retail employee or a rural carrier; USPS employees may not prepare or seal the mail; the full value must be declared; domestic Registered Mail is available with First-Class Mail, USPS Ground Advantage and Priority Mail, and it is slower. Tracking and delivery: USPS gives customers no facility-to-facility updates for Registered Mail alone; delivery information appears when a scan shows a delivery or an attempted delivery; the internal receipts are not readily available and are reached only by starting a claim form; proof of delivery with a signature comes from a Return Receipt bought at mailing. If it is lost: the Registered Mail fee is not refunded, postage is refunded if a claim is made; for Registered Mail with no declared value, the DMM has a separate mailer inquiry after 15 days from mailing. The 14 and 15 days are different procedures: the Missing Mail FAQ says to allow 14 or more days before a search request and/or a claim, and the pages do not tie the two numbers together or to the claim filing period.
svg.text: USPS Registered Mail
What the USPS pages say
1. What it is
The most secure USPS mail service: safes,
cages, sealed containers, locks and keys.
A signature is required on delivery.
Restricted Delivery directs delivery only
to the addressee or authorized agent.
2. Sending it
Only at the time of mailing; presented to
a retail employee or a rural carrier. USPS
employees may not prepare or seal it.
Declare the full value. Available with
First-Class Mail, Ground Advantage and
Priority Mail; slower, not for speed.
3. Tracking and delivery
No facility-to-facility updates for customers.
Delivery information appears when a scan
shows a delivery or an attempted delivery.
Internal receipts are not readily available;
a claim form reaches them. A signed record
of delivery comes from a Return Receipt.
4. If it is lost
The Registered Mail fee is not refunded;
postage is refunded if a claim is made.
No declared value: the DMM has a separate
mailer inquiry after 15 days from mailing.
Where the pages differ
14 or more days (Missing Mail FAQ: search
request and/or claim) and 15 days (DMM:
mailer inquiry, no declared value) are
different procedures; the pages do not
tie them together. Eligible classes: the
FAQ lists four; the DMM points to an exhibit.
Sources: USPS FAQs 000006061, 000007968;
DMM 503 section 2.0; read Nov. 24, 2026
